records.source: וּבִשְׁנֵים֩ עָשָׂ֨ר חֹ֜דֶשׁ הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֗ר בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ בּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִגִּ֧יעַ דְּבַר־הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְדָת֖וֹ לְהֵעָשׂ֑וֹת בַּיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שִׂבְּר֜וּ אֹיְבֵ֤י הַיְּהוּדִים֙ לִשְׁל֣וֹט בָּהֶ֔ם וְנַהֲפ֣וֹךְ ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלְט֧וּ הַיְּהוּדִ֛ים הֵ֖מָּה בְּשֹׂנְאֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And in [the] twelfth month, that [is the] month Adar, on [the] thirteenth day in it, when drew near [the] word of the king and his law to be done, on the day when had hoped [the] enemies of the Jews to gain power over them, and it was turned around, that ruled the Jews, they, over [those] hating them,
pieces: In the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on its thirteenth day, the king's command and his decree were due to be carried out. On the very day when the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, the opposite happened: the Jews overpowered those who hated them.

L.1: And in the twelfth month, which [is] the month Adar, on its thirteenth day, when the word of the king and his law drew near to be carried out, on the day when the enemies of the Jews had hoped to gain power over them, it was turned around: the Jews themselves gained power over those who hated them.

R.1: The king's order was to be carried out on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar. On that day the enemies of the Jews had hoped to defeat them. But everything was turned around, and the Jews defeated the people who hated them.

decisions.choice: the thirteenth of Adar: the day fixed by Haman's lot and by both decrees
decisions.reason: This is the day the lot fell on when Haman planned the killing (3:7, 13), and the same day Mordecai's later decree gave the Jews the right to defend themselves (8:12). Adar is the twelfth month of the year, in late winter (February to March).

decisions.choice: it was turned around: the expected outcome was reversed
decisions.reason: The verb means to overturn or turn upside down. It names the pattern of the whole book, where every threat against the Jews comes back on its maker: Haman is hanged on the gallows he built (7:10), and the month of grief becomes a month of joy (9:22, where the same verb returns).

decisions.choice: gain power over: to get control of, to overpower
decisions.reason: The verb means to rule or have mastery over someone. It is used twice here, of what the enemies hoped and of what the Jews did, so the sentence itself shows the reversal.

decisions.choice: one long Hebrew sentence split into two or three English sentences
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up time phrases before its main statement. Balanced and Readable state the date first and then the reversal, so the sentence can be read aloud.

records.heading: The day that was turned around

records.source: נִקְהֲל֨וּ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים בְּעָרֵיהֶ֗ם בְּכָל־מְדִינוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֳחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ יָ֔ד בִּמְבַקְשֵׁ֖י רָֽעָתָ֑ם וְאִישׁ֙ לֹא־עָמַ֣ד לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־נָפַ֥ל פַּחְדָּ֖ם עַל־כָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Assembled the Jews in their cities in all [the] provinces of the king Ahasuerus to stretch out [a] hand on [those] seeking their harm; and [a] man not stood before them, for had fallen [the] dread of them on all the peoples.
pieces: The Jews gathered in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to attack those who were seeking to harm them. No one could stand against them, because fear of them had fallen on all the peoples.

L.2: The Jews assembled in their cities in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to lay a hand on those who sought their harm; and no one stood before them, for the dread of them had fallen on all the peoples.

R.2: In all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, the Jews gathered in their cities to fight the people who wanted to hurt them. No one could stand up against them, because all the other peoples were afraid of them.

decisions.choice: stretch out a hand on: to attack
decisions.reason: To stretch out the hand against someone means to lay hands on them in violence (2:21; 3:6; 8:7).

decisions.choice: those seeking their harm: the attack was on those who meant to harm them
decisions.reason: The text names the targets as people who were seeking the Jews' harm, in line with the king's second decree, which allowed the Jews to defend themselves against any force that attacked them (8:11).

decisions.choice: no man stood before them: no one could withstand them
decisions.reason: To stand before someone in battle means to hold one's ground against them (Joshua 1:5; 10:8).

decisions.choice: attack (B); fight (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom of the hand is put into plain words at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "lay a hand on".

records.source: וְכָל־שָׂרֵ֨י הַמְּדִינ֜וֹת וְהָאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִ֣ים וְהַפַּח֗וֹת וְעֹשֵׂ֤י הַמְּלָאכָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מְנַשְּׂאִ֖ים אֶת־הַיְּהוּדִ֑ים כִּֽי־נָפַ֥ל פַּֽחַד־מָרְדֳּכַ֖י עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And all [the] princes of the provinces and the satraps and the governors and [the] doers of the work that [belonged] to the king [were] lifting up the Jews, for had fallen [the] dread of Mordecai on them.
pieces: All the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors and the king's administrators supported the Jews, because fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.

L.3: And all the princes of the provinces and the satraps and the governors and those who did the king's business were supporting the Jews, for the dread of Mordecai had fallen on them.

R.3: All the leaders of the provinces, the regional governors, the local governors and the king's officials helped the Jews, because they were afraid of Mordecai.

decisions.choice: satraps and governors: the ranks of Persian provincial government
decisions.reason: Satraps ruled the large regions of the empire, and governors ruled smaller provinces under them; the same ranks receive the king's letters in 3:12 and 8:9.

decisions.choice: doers of the king's work: the royal administrators
decisions.reason: The phrase means the officials who handled the king's affairs and treasury, as in 3:9, where Haman offers to pay silver into their hands.

decisions.choice: lifting up: supporting, helping
decisions.reason: The verb lift up is used here in the sense of giving support, as in Ezra 1:4 and 8:36, where officials "lift up" the people and the house of God with help.

decisions.choice: regional governors and local governors
decisions.reason: Readable uses "regional governors" for satraps, as elsewhere in Esther, and "local governors" for the lower rank so the two stay distinct.

records.source: כִּֽי־גָ֤דוֹל מָרְדֳּכַי֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְשָׁמְע֖וֹ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּכָל־הַמְּדִינ֑וֹת כִּֽי־הָאִ֥ישׁ מָרְדֳּכַ֖י הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֽוֹל׃פ
records.gloss: For great [was] Mordecai in [the] house of the king, and his fame [was] going in all the provinces, for the man Mordecai [was] going and becoming great.
pieces: For Mordecai was powerful in the king's palace, and his fame spread through all the provinces; the man Mordecai grew more and more powerful.

L.4: For Mordecai was great in the house of the king, and his fame was going out through all the provinces, for the man Mordecai was growing greater and greater.

R.4: Mordecai had become an important man in the king's palace. People in all the provinces heard about him, and he kept getting more and more powerful.

decisions.choice: going and becoming great: growing steadily greater
decisions.reason: The verb go with another verb marks something that keeps on increasing, as David "went on growing stronger" (2 Samuel 3:1; 5:10).

decisions.choice: the house of the king: the royal court
decisions.reason: The king's house is the palace and the court around it, where Mordecai now holds Haman's former place (8:2).

decisions.choice: powerful (B); important, powerful (R)
decisions.reason: "Great" here is about rank and influence, so Balanced and Readable say "powerful"; Literal keeps "great".

records.source: וַיַּכּ֤וּ הַיְּהוּדִים֙ בְּכָל־אֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם מַכַּת־חֶ֥רֶב וְהֶ֖רֶג וְאַבְדָ֑ן וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֥וּ בְשֹׂנְאֵיהֶ֖ם כִּרְצוֹנָֽם׃
records.gloss: And struck the Jews all their enemies [with a] blow of sword and killing and destruction, and they did with [those] hating them according to their will.
pieces: The Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying them, and they did as they pleased to those who hated them.

L.5: And the Jews struck all their enemies with a blow of the sword, with killing and destruction, and they did to those who hated them as they pleased.

R.5: The Jews attacked all their enemies with swords and killed them. They did whatever they wanted to the people who hated them.

decisions.choice: sword, killing and destruction: the words of the decrees turned back
decisions.reason: Haman's decree ordered the Jews "to be destroyed, killed and wiped out" (3:13; 7:4), and Mordecai's answered it in the same words (8:11). Here the words describe what happened to the enemies instead.

decisions.choice: according to their will: as they wished
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of the guests at the king's feast drinking as each one wished (1:8). It means the Jews were free to act; the text does not add a judgment on how they acted.

decisions.choice: with swords and killed them
decisions.reason: Readable merges the three nouns into one plain statement; the repeated words are kept at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: וּבְשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֗ה הָרְג֤וּ הַיְּהוּדִים֙ וְאַבֵּ֔ד חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And in Susa the citadel killed the Jews and destroyed five hundred men.
pieces: In the citadel of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed 500 men.

L.6: And in Susa the citadel the Jews killed and destroyed 500 men.

R.6: In the royal fortress in Susa, the Jews killed 500 men.

decisions.choice: Susa the citadel: the fortified royal quarter of Susa
decisions.reason: The citadel is the fortified palace area of the capital. The text later speaks of the Jews "in Susa" more widely (9:13-15), so the count here is for the citadel.

decisions.choice: killed (for "killed and destroyed")
decisions.reason: The two verbs say one thing with emphasis; Readable uses one.

records.source: וְאֵ֧ת׀פַּרְשַׁנְדָּ֛תָא וְאֵ֥ת׀דַּֽלְפ֖וֹן וְאֵ֥ת׀אַסְפָּֽתָא׃
records.gloss: And Parshandatha and Dalphon and Aspatha,
pieces: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

L.7: And Parshandatha and Dalphon and Aspatha,

R.7: They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

decisions.choice: the ten names: set out in a column in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: Verses 7-9 list Haman's ten sons. In the Hebrew manuscripts and in Jewish scrolls of Esther the names are written in a column, each on its own line, and the verb that governs them comes only in verse 10 ("they killed"). The names are Persian; their meanings are not certain.

decisions.choice: They also killed ... (verb brought forward from verse 10)
decisions.reason: Hebrew keeps the verb to the end of the list in verse 10. Balanced and Readable say it at the start so the list can be followed; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

records.source: וְאֵ֧ת׀פּוֹרָ֛תָא וְאֵ֥ת׀אֲדַלְיָ֖א וְאֵ֥ת׀אֲרִידָֽתָא׃
records.gloss: and Poratha and Adalia and Aridatha,
pieces: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

L.8: and Poratha and Adalia and Aridatha,

decisions.choice: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha: three more of Haman's sons
decisions.reason: The list continues from verse 7 and runs to verse 10. The spellings follow the Hebrew.

records.source: וְאֵ֤ת׀פַּרְמַ֨שְׁתָּא֙ וְאֵ֣ת׀אֲרִיסַ֔י וְאֵ֥ת׀אֲרִדַ֖י וְאֵ֥ת׀וַיְזָֽתָא׃
records.gloss: and Parmashta and Arisai and Aridai and Vaizatha,
pieces: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha,

L.9: and Parmashta and Arisai and Aridai and Vaizatha,

decisions.choice: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, Vaizatha: the last four of the ten
decisions.reason: These complete the ten names begun in verse 7. In the traditional Hebrew text some letters in these names are written smaller or larger than the rest (as in Vaizatha), a scribal feature that does not change the meaning.

records.source: עֲ֠שֶׂרֶת בְּנֵ֨י הָמָ֧ן בֶּֽן־הַמְּדָ֛תָא צֹרֵ֥ר הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים הָרָ֑גוּ וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־יָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: [the] ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, [the] harasser of the Jews, they killed; and on the plunder not they stretched out their hand.
pieces: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay a hand on the plunder.

L.10: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews, they killed; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.

R.10: the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not take anything for themselves from the people they killed.

decisions.choice: the harasser of the Jews: the one who oppressed and opposed them
decisions.reason: The word describes someone who hems in and attacks; it is Haman's title in 3:10 and 8:1 and again in 9:24.

decisions.choice: they did not take plunder, though the decree allowed it
decisions.reason: Mordecai's decree permitted the Jews to take the goods of those who attacked them (8:11), yet they took nothing, and the text says so three times (9:10, 15, 16). If Haman the Agagite is read as a descendant of Agag king of Amalek (3:1), this answers King Saul, who took the spoil of the Amalekites against the LORD's command (1 Samuel 15:9, 19). The text invites this reading but does not state it.

decisions.choice: did not take anything for themselves from the people they killed
decisions.reason: Readable explains what plunder is; the sense is the same.

records.source: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא בָּ֣א מִסְפַּ֧ר הַֽהֲרוּגִ֛ים בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
records.gloss: On the day the that came [the] number of the killed in Susa the citadel before the king.
pieces: That same day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king.

L.11: On that day the number of those killed in Susa the citadel came before the king.

R.11: That day the king was told how many people had been killed in the royal fortress in Susa.

decisions.choice: came before the king: was reported to him
decisions.reason: To come before the king is to be brought to his notice, as reports and requests are in 1:19 and 9:25.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֗ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֡ה הָרְגוּ֩ הַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְאַבֵּ֜ד חֲמֵ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ וְאֵת֙ עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת בְּנֵֽי־הָמָ֔ן בִּשְׁאָ֛ר מְדִינ֥וֹת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מֶ֣ה עָשׂ֑וּ וּמַה־שְּׁאֵֽלָתֵךְ֙ וְיִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֔ךְ וּמַה־בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֥ךְ ע֖וֹד וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃
records.gloss: And said the king to Esther the queen, in Susa the citadel have killed the Jews and destroyed five hundred men and [the] ten sons of Haman; in [the] rest of [the] provinces of the king what have they done? And what [is] your petition? And it will be given to you. And what [is] your request further? And it will be done.
pieces: The king said to Queen Esther, "In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed 500 men and the ten sons of Haman. What must they have done in the rest of the king's provinces! Now what is your petition? It will be granted you. What else do you ask? It will be done."

L.12: And the king said to Queen Esther, "In Susa the citadel the Jews have killed and destroyed 500 men and the ten sons of Haman. In the rest of the king's provinces, what have they done! And what is your petition? It shall be given to you. And what more is your request? It shall be done."

R.12: The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews have killed 500 men in the royal fortress in Susa, and also Haman's ten sons. They must have killed many more in the rest of my provinces! Now what else do you want? I will give it to you. Tell me what you ask for, and it will be done."

decisions.choice: what have they done: an exclamation, not a request for figures
alternatives: a real question: what have they done in the other provinces?
decisions.reason: The question has no answer in the text and the king goes straight on to Esther's wish. It means: if this happened in Susa alone, think how much they have done in the rest of the provinces.

decisions.choice: your petition, your request: the king's words at Esther's earlier feasts
decisions.reason: The king offers again in the same words he used at both of Esther's banquets (5:6; 7:2). Then she asked for her life; now he asks what more she wants.

decisions.choice: my provinces
decisions.reason: The king speaks of himself as "the king"; Readable says "my" so the reader does not wonder who is meant.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶסְתֵּר֙ אִם־עַל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ ט֔וֹב יִנָּתֵ֣ן גַּם־מָחָ֗ר לַיְּהוּדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשׁוּשָׁ֔ן לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כְּדָ֣ת הַיּ֑וֹם וְאֵ֛ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת בְּנֵֽי־הָמָ֖ן יִתְל֥וּ עַל־הָעֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: And said Esther, if on the king [it is] good, let it be given also tomorrow to the Jews who [are] in Susa to do according to [the] law of today; and [the] ten sons of Haman let them hang on the gallows.
pieces: Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa be allowed to act tomorrow too, as today's decree allows, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows."

L.13: And Esther said, "If it is good to the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Susa to act tomorrow also according to today's law, and let them hang the ten sons of Haman on the gallows."

R.13: Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa do again tomorrow what the law let them do today. And let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows."

decisions.choice: to act tomorrow according to today's law: the permission extended by one day in Susa
decisions.reason: The king's second decree allowed the Jews to defend themselves on the thirteenth of Adar only (8:11-12). Esther asks that the same permission hold in Susa for the fourteenth, which is why the Jews of Susa keep the feast a day later (9:18).

decisions.choice: hang the ten sons: display the bodies of men already dead
decisions.reason: The sons were already killed (9:10). Hanging the bodies in public was a mark of disgrace and a warning to others (1 Samuel 31:10; Deuteronomy 21:22-23). They are hanged on the gallows their father had prepared (5:14; 7:10).

decisions.choice: the gallows: a tall wooden pole
decisions.reason: The word means tree or wood. In Esther it is the pole Haman set up, fifty cubits high (5:14). Whether bodies were hanged from it or fixed on it as a stake is not certain.

decisions.choice: If it pleases the king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "if on the king [it is] good", the polite form of a request to a king (1:19; 5:4; 8:5). Literal keeps "good to the king".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְהֵֽעָשׂ֣וֹת כֵּ֔ן וַתִּנָּתֵ֥ן דָּ֖ת בְּשׁוּשָׁ֑ן וְאֵ֛ת עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת בְּנֵֽי־הָמָ֖ן תָּלֽוּ׃
records.gloss: And said the king to be done thus, and was given [the] law in Susa, and [the] ten sons of Haman they hanged.
pieces: So the king ordered that this be done. A decree was issued in Susa, and the ten sons of Haman were hanged.

L.14: And the king said for it to be done so; and a law was given out in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.

R.14: So the king ordered it to be done. A law was announced in Susa, and Haman's ten sons were hanged.

decisions.choice: they hanged: an impersonal plural, "were hanged"
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; it means the order was carried out by those responsible, as also in 9:25.

decisions.choice: a law was given: a decree was published
decisions.reason: To give a law is to issue it publicly, as in 3:14-15 and 8:13-14.

records.source: וַיִּֽקָּהֲל֞וּ הַיְּהוּדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן גַּ֠ם בְּי֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר וַיַּֽהַרְג֣וּ בְשׁוּשָׁ֔ן שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת אִ֑ישׁ וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־יָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And assembled the Jews who [were] in Susa also on [the] fourteenth day of [the] month Adar, and they killed in Susa three hundred men; and on the plunder not they stretched out their hand.
pieces: The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of the month Adar and killed 300 men in Susa. But they did not lay a hand on the plunder.

L.15: And the Jews who were in Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and they killed in Susa 300 men; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.

R.15: The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of Adar, and they killed 300 men in the city. But they did not take anything for themselves.

decisions.choice: also on the fourteenth: the second day granted at Esther's request
decisions.reason: This carries out the extra day of verse 13. The figure of 300 is for the city of Susa beyond the citadel count of verse 6.

decisions.choice: they did not lay their hand on the plunder
decisions.reason: The second of three such statements (9:10, 16); see the decision at 9:10.

records.source: וּשְׁאָ֣ר הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים אֲשֶׁר֩ בִּמְדִינ֨וֹת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ נִקְהֲל֣וּ׀וְעָמֹ֣ד עַל־נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְנ֨וֹחַ֙ מֵאֹ֣יְבֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָרֹג֙ בְּשֹׂ֣נְאֵיהֶ֔ם חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה וְשִׁבְעִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף וּבַ֨בִּזָּ֔ה לֹ֥א שָֽׁלְח֖וּ אֶת־יָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of the Jews who [were] in [the] provinces of the king assembled and stood for their life, and rested from their enemies, and killed among [those] hating them five and seventy thousand; and on the plunder not they stretched out their hand.
pieces: Meanwhile the rest of the Jews in the king's provinces gathered to defend their lives, and they had rest from their enemies. They killed 75,000 of those who hated them, but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.

L.16: And the rest of the Jews who were in the king's provinces assembled and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and killed 75,000 of those who hated them; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.

R.16: At the same time, the other Jews in the king's provinces gathered to protect themselves, and they were set free from their enemies. They killed 75,000 of the people who hated them. But they did not take anything for themselves.

decisions.choice: stood for their life: defended themselves
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats the wording of the king's second decree (8:11), which allowed the Jews to stand up for their lives.

decisions.choice: rested from their enemies: were relieved of them, had peace from them
decisions.reason: Rest here is safety from attack, as the land had rest from enemies under the judges and David (Joshua 21:44; 2 Samuel 7:1). The same rest is what the feast remembers (9:17-18, 22).

decisions.choice: seventy-five thousand (the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has 75,000. The old Greek translation of Esther has 15,000. The Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: they were set free from their enemies
decisions.reason: Readable puts "rested from" in plain words; the sense is relief from attack (m2).

records.source: בְּיוֹם־שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֑ר וְנ֗וֹחַ בְּאַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וְעָשֹׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ י֖וֹם מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה וְשִׂמְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: On [the] thirteenth day of [the] month Adar; and resting on [the] fourteenth in it, and making it a day of feasting and joy.
pieces: This was on the thirteenth day of the month Adar. On the fourteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.

L.17: [This was] on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and they rested on its fourteenth and made it a day of feasting and joy.

R.17: This happened on the thirteenth day of Adar. On the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and joy.

decisions.choice: On the thirteenth: dating the fighting in the provinces of verse 16
decisions.reason: The verse begins with a bare date. It ties the fighting of verse 16 to the thirteenth, and the rest and feast to the next day, in contrast with Susa (verse 18).

decisions.choice: a day of feasting and joy
decisions.reason: The word for feast is the one used for drinking banquets throughout the book: the king's feasts (1:3, 5) and Esther's (5:4; 7:2). The book that began with the king's feasting ends with the Jews' own.

decisions.choice: [This was] (L); This was (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew date stands with no verb; English supplies one.

records.source: וְהַיְּהוּדִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־בְּשׁוּשָׁ֗ן נִקְהֲלוּ֙ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וּבְאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר בּ֑וֹ וְנ֗וֹחַ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ בּ֔וֹ וְעָשֹׂ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ י֖וֹם מִשְׁתֶּ֥ה וְשִׂמְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the Jews who [were] in Susa assembled on [the] thirteenth in it and on [the] fourteenth in it, and resting on [the] fifteenth in it, and making it a day of feasting and joy.
pieces: But the Jews in Susa had gathered on both the thirteenth and the fourteenth, so they rested on the fifteenth and made it a day of feasting and joy.

L.18: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled on its thirteenth and on its fourteenth, and they rested on its fifteenth and made it a day of feasting and joy.

R.18: But the Jews in Susa had gathered to fight on both the thirteenth and the fourteenth. So they rested on the fifteenth and made that their day of feasting and joy.

decisions.choice: Susa's feast on the fifteenth
decisions.reason: Because the fighting in Susa lasted two days (9:13-15), the Jews there rested a day later. This is the origin of the two dates in verses 19 and 21; Jewish practice still keeps Purim on the fifteenth in walled cities and on the fourteenth elsewhere.

decisions.choice: gathered to fight
decisions.reason: Readable says why they gathered, as verses 2 and 15 make clear.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֞ן הַיְּהוּדִ֣ים הַפְּרָזִ֗ים הַיֹּשְׁבִים֮ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַפְּרָזוֹת֒ עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֠ת י֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר שִׂמְחָ֥ה וּמִשְׁתֶּ֖ה וְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב וּמִשְׁל֥וֹחַ מָנ֖וֹת אִ֥ישׁ לְרֵעֵֽהוּ׃פ
records.gloss: Therefore the Jews, the villagers who dwell in [the] cities of the open country, [are] making [the] fourteenth day of [the] month Adar joy and feasting and a good day, and sending portions each to his neighbor.
pieces: That is why the Jews of the villages, who live in unwalled towns, keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar as a day of joy and feasting, a holiday, when they send gifts of food to one another.

L.19: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar [a day of] joy and feasting and a good day, and of sending portions {{gender:each one to their neighbor|each man to his neighbor}}.

R.19: That is why Jews who live in villages and towns without walls celebrate on the fourteenth day of Adar. It is a happy holiday with feasting, and people send gifts of food to each other.

decisions.choice: villagers in the towns of the open country: Jews in unwalled settlements
decisions.reason: The words describe open country and towns without walls (Deuteronomy 3:5; Ezekiel 38:11), in contrast with fortified Susa. The Hebrew has two spellings of the first word in the written and the read text; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a good day: a festival, a holiday
decisions.reason: A good day is a day of celebration (8:17; 1 Samuel 25:8).

decisions.choice: sending portions: giving gifts of food
decisions.reason: Portions are shares of food from a feast, sent to others (Nehemiah 8:10, 12). The present tense ("make") speaks from the writer's own time, when the custom was already kept.

decisions.choice: each one to their neighbor / each man to his neighbor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew idiom means one another, men and women alike, so Literal uses the gender setting; Balanced and Readable say "one another".

records.source: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מָרְדֳּכַ֔י אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סְפָרִ֜ים אֶל־כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּכָל־מְדִינוֹת֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ הַקְּרוֹבִ֖ים וְהָרְחוֹקִֽים׃
records.gloss: And wrote Mordecai the words the these, and sent letters to all the Jews who [were] in all [the] provinces of the king Ahasuerus, the near and the far,
pieces: Mordecai recorded these events, and he sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far,

L.20: And Mordecai wrote these things and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far,

R.20: Mordecai wrote down what had happened. He sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, near and far.

decisions.choice: wrote these things: recorded the events just told
alternatives: wrote these words (the letter that follows)
decisions.reason: The words can mean these events or these words. Most likely Mordecai wrote down what had happened as the ground for the feast; it may also mean the instructions that follow in his letters.

decisions.choice: a full stop at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 21. Readable ends it here and begins verse 21 with "He told them".

records.heading: Mordecai's letter and the days of Purim

records.source: לְקַיֵּם֮ עֲלֵיהֶם֒ לִהְי֣וֹת עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֠ת י֣וֹם אַרְבָּעָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ לְחֹ֣דֶשׁ אֲדָ֔ר וְאֵ֛ת יוֹם־חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר בּ֑וֹ בְּכָל־שָׁנָ֖ה וְשָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: to establish on them to be observing [the] fourteenth day of [the] month Adar and [the] fifteenth day in it, in every year and year,
pieces: to require them to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar every year,

L.21: to establish for them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar and its fifteenth day, every year,

R.21: He told them to celebrate the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar every year.

decisions.choice: to establish on them: to make it binding on them
decisions.reason: The verb means to set up or confirm, and with "on them" to make something a fixed duty. It is the key word of the chapter's ending (9:27, 29, 31, 32).

decisions.choice: the fourteenth and the fifteenth: both days of the feast
alternatives: every Jew to keep both days
decisions.reason: The letter names both days. Read with verses 18-19, it fixes the fourteenth for the villages and the fifteenth for Susa; it may also mean that both days were to be kept by all.

decisions.choice: He told them
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence here (see 9:20) and supplies a subject and verb.

records.source: כַּיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־נָ֨חוּ בָהֶ֤ם הַיְּהוּדִים֙ מֵא֣וֹיְבֵיהֶ֔ם וְהַחֹ֗דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר֩ נֶהְפַּ֨ךְ לָהֶ֤ם מִיָּגוֹן֙ לְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּמֵאֵ֖בֶל לְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אוֹתָ֗ם יְמֵי֙ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה וְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּמִשְׁל֤וֹחַ מָנוֹת֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וּמַתָּנ֖וֹת לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִֽים׃
records.gloss: as [the] days on which had rest the Jews from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day; to make them days of feasting and joy and sending portions each to his neighbor and gifts to the poor.
pieces: as the days when the Jews got rest from their enemies, and as the month that was turned for them from grief into joy and from mourning into a holiday. They were to make them days of feasting and joy, of sending gifts of food to one another and gifts to the poor.

L.22: as the days on which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month that was turned for them from sorrow into joy and from mourning into a good day; to make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions {{gender:each one to their neighbor|each man to his neighbor}}, and gifts to the poor.

R.22: These were the days when the Jews were set free from their enemies. That month their sadness turned into joy, and their mourning into a holiday. So they were to celebrate with feasts and joy, send gifts of food to each other, and give gifts to poor people.

decisions.choice: turned from sorrow to joy and from mourning to a good day
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the great reversal in 9:1. The month of Adar had been the month of fasting and sackcloth when Haman's decree came (4:1-3); now it becomes a month of celebration.

decisions.choice: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Along with feasting and gifts of food to friends, the feast includes care for the poor, a custom of Purim still kept.

decisions.choice: a new sentence for "to make them days of feasting"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs from verse 20 through this verse. Balanced and Readable break it so it can be followed.

records.source: וְקִבֵּל֙ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־הֵחֵ֖לּוּ לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־כָּתַ֥ב מָרְדֳּכַ֖י אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And accepted the Jews what they had begun to do, and what had written Mordecai to them.
pieces: So the Jews made a custom of what they had begun to do, and of what Mordecai had written to them.

L.23: And the Jews accepted what they had begun to do, and what Mordecai had written to them.

R.23: So the Jews agreed to keep on doing what they had started to do, as Mordecai had written to them.

decisions.choice: accepted: took on as a binding custom
decisions.reason: The verb means to receive or take upon oneself. The feast began with what the Jews did of their own accord (9:17-19), and Mordecai's letter made it a fixed practice; the people accepted both. The same verb returns in 9:27.

decisions.choice: made a custom of
decisions.reason: "Accepted" alone could sound like mere agreement; Balanced says what the Jews took on.

records.source: כִּי֩ הָמָ֨ן בֶּֽן־הַמְּדָ֜תָא הָֽאֲגָגִ֗י צֹרֵר֙ כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים חָשַׁ֥ב עַל־הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים לְאַבְּדָ֑ם וְהִפִּ֥יל פּוּר֙ ה֣וּא הַגּוֹרָ֔ל לְהֻמָּ֖ם וּֽלְאַבְּדָֽם׃
records.gloss: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, [the] harasser of all the Jews, had planned against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur, that [is] the lot, to throw them into confusion and to destroy them.
pieces: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them. He had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to crush and destroy them.

L.24: For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to crush them and to destroy them.

R.24: This was because Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had made plans to destroy them. He had cast Pur (that is, the lot) to choose the day to crush them and destroy them.

decisions.choice: Pur, that is, the lot
decisions.reason: Pur is a foreign word, from the Akkadian language of Babylon, for a lot used to decide something by chance. The writer explains it with the ordinary Hebrew word for lot, as in 3:7, where Haman had the lot cast to choose the month and day of the killing. The feast takes its name from it (verse 26).

decisions.choice: to throw them into confusion: to crush them
decisions.reason: The verb means to rout or throw into panic, a word used for the LORD routing an enemy army (Exodus 14:24; Joshua 10:10). It sounds like Haman's own name, which may be a play on words; the text does not point it out.

decisions.choice: the Agagite
decisions.reason: See the decision at 3:1 on the link with Agag king of Amalek. Here at the end, the whole of Haman's plot is summed up in one sentence.

decisions.choice: to choose the day
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lot was for, as 3:7 tells; the Hebrew here leaves it implied.

records.source: וּבְבֹאָהּ֮ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ אָמַ֣ר עִם־הַסֵּ֔פֶר יָשׁ֞וּב מַחֲשַׁבְתּ֧וֹ הָרָעָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־חָשַׁ֥ב עַל־הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וְתָל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו עַל־הָעֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: And when she came before the king, he said with the letter, let return his plan the evil which he had planned against the Jews on his head; and they hanged him and his sons on the gallows.
pieces: But when Esther came before the king, he gave orders in writing that the evil plan Haman had plotted against the Jews should fall back on his own head, and Haman and his sons were hanged on the gallows.

L.25: But when she came before the king, he said by letter that his evil plan which he had plotted against the Jews should return on his own head, and they hanged him and his sons on the gallows.

R.25: But when Esther went to the king, the king gave orders in writing. The evil plan that Haman had made against the Jews would happen to Haman himself instead. So Haman and his sons were hanged on the gallows.

decisions.choice: when she came: when Esther came before the king
alternatives: when the matter came before the king
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "when she (or it) came before the king". It most likely means Esther, who went to the king (5:1-2; 8:3); it can also mean "when the matter came before the king".

decisions.choice: return on his head: come back on the one who planned it
decisions.reason: To have one's evil return on one's own head is to suffer the harm one meant for others (1 Kings 2:44; Psalm 7:17). This is the reversal of 9:1 in Haman's own life.

decisions.choice: he said with the letter: he gave written orders
decisions.reason: This is a short summary of chapters 7-8. Haman's hanging was ordered by word of mouth (7:9), and the letters reversing his plot were sent afterward (8:8-10); the verse puts the king's orders together.

decisions.choice: Esther; Haman
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people the Hebrew pronouns point to, following m1.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֡ן קָֽרְאוּ֩ לַיָּמִ֨ים הָאֵ֤לֶּה פוּרִים֙ עַל־שֵׁ֣ם הַפּ֔וּר עַל־כֵּ֕ן עַל־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הָאִגֶּ֣רֶת הַזֹּ֑את וּמָֽה־רָא֣וּ עַל־כָּ֔כָה וּמָ֥ה הִגִּ֖יעַ אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Therefore they called the days the these Purim, on [the] name of the Pur; therefore, because of all [the] words of the letter the this, and what they had seen concerning this, and what had come to them,
pieces: That is why these days are called Purim, from the word Pur. And so, because of everything written in this letter, and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,

L.26: Therefore they called these days Purim, after the name of Pur. Therefore, because of all the words of this letter, and of what they had seen concerning this, and what had come upon them,

R.26: That is why these days are called Purim, from the word Pur, which means "lot". Because of everything in Mordecai's letter, and because of all that they had seen and all that had happened to them,

decisions.choice: Purim: the plural of Pur, "lots"
decisions.reason: The feast is named after the lot Haman cast to fix the day for destroying the Jews (3:7; 9:24). The day chosen for their death became the day of their rescue.

decisions.choice: this letter: Mordecai's letter of verse 20
decisions.reason: The letter is the one Mordecai sent to all the provinces (9:20-22).

decisions.choice: what they had seen concerning this: what they had lived through
decisions.reason: The Jews keep the feast both because of the letter and because of their own experience of the danger and the rescue.

decisions.choice: Mordecai's letter; which means "lot"
decisions.reason: Readable names whose letter it was and repeats the meaning of Pur from 9:24.

records.source: קִיְּמ֣וּ וְקִבְּל֣וּהַיְּהוּדִים֩׀עֲלֵיהֶ֨ם׀וְעַל־זַרְעָ֜ם וְעַ֨ל כָּל־הַנִּלְוִ֤ים עֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲב֔וֹר לִהְי֣וֹת עֹשִׂ֗ים אֵ֣ת שְׁנֵ֤י הַיָּמִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה כִּכְתָבָ֖ם וְכִזְמַנָּ֑ם בְּכָל־שָׁנָ֖ה וְשָׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: established and accepted the Jews on themselves and on their offspring and on all [those] joining themselves to them, and it will not pass away, to be observing [the] two the days the these according to their writing and according to their appointed time in every year and year.
pieces: the Jews made it a binding custom for themselves, for their descendants and for all who joined them, that without fail they would keep these two days, as it was written and at the appointed time every year.

L.27: the Jews established and took upon themselves and upon their descendants and upon all who joined themselves to them, so that it should not pass away, to keep these two days as it was written about them and at their appointed time, every year.

R.27: the Jews made it a rule for themselves, for their descendants and for everyone who joined them. They would never stop celebrating these two days every year in the way that was written and at the right time.

decisions.choice: all who joined themselves to them: people of other nations who joined the Jews
decisions.reason: The words describe outsiders who attached themselves to the Jewish people and its God, like the many who became Jews in 8:17 (see also Isaiah 56:3, 6).

decisions.choice: established and accepted: made a binding rule and took it on
decisions.reason: The two verbs from verses 21 and 23 come together: what was set up for the Jews they now take upon themselves. The written Hebrew text has the second verb in the singular, the text read aloud in the plural; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: according to their writing and their time: as written, on the set dates
decisions.reason: The days are to be kept as the letters described them (9:20-22) and on their fixed dates, the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar.

decisions.choice: without fail; never stop
decisions.reason: "It will not pass away" means the practice must never lapse; Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

records.source: וְהַיָּמִ֣ים הָ֠אֵלֶּה נִזְכָּרִ֨ים וְנַעֲשִׂ֜ים בְּכָל־דּ֣וֹר וָד֗וֹר מִשְׁפָּחָה֙ וּמִשְׁפָּחָ֔ה מְדִינָ֥ה וּמְדִינָ֖ה וְעִ֣יר וָעִ֑יר וִימֵ֞י הַפּוּרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה לֹ֤א יַֽעַבְרוּ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְזִכְרָ֖ם לֹא־יָס֥וּף מִזַּרְעָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And the days the these [are] remembered and done in every generation and generation, clan and clan, province and province, and city and city; and [the] days of the Purim the these will not pass away from among the Jews, and their remembrance will not come to an end from their offspring.
pieces: These days are to be remembered and kept in every generation, by every clan, in every province and in every city. These days of Purim must never disappear from among the Jews, and the memory of them must never fade among their descendants.

L.28: And these days are to be remembered and kept in every generation, every clan, every province and every city; and these days of Purim shall not pass away from among the Jews, and the memory of them shall not come to an end among their descendants.

R.28: These days must be remembered and celebrated in every generation, by every family, in every province and in every city. The Jews must never stop keeping these days of Purim, and their descendants must always remember them.

decisions.choice: remembered and done: are to be remembered and kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses participles, which here describe a lasting rule for the future.

decisions.choice: generation and generation, clan and clan: every generation, every clan
decisions.reason: Repeating a noun is the Hebrew way of saying "every"; the list moves from time (generations) to people (clans) to places (provinces and cities).

decisions.choice: their remembrance: the memory of these days
decisions.reason: The feast exists so that the rescue is remembered. The verb for coming to an end means to cease or be finished.

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for clan, as elsewhere.

records.source: וַ֠תִּכְתֹּב אֶסְתֵּ֨ר הַמַּלְכָּ֧ה בַת־אֲבִיחַ֛יִל וּמָרְדֳּכַ֥י הַיְּהוּדִ֖י אֶת־כָּל־תֹּ֑קֶף לְקַיֵּ֗ם אֵ֣ת אִגֶּ֧רֶת הַפּוּרִ֛ים הַזֹּ֖את הַשֵּׁנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And wrote Esther the queen, [the] daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew, with all authority, to confirm the letter of the Purim the this, the second.
pieces: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim.

L.29: And Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

R.29: Then Queen Esther, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote a second letter about Purim. They used all their authority to make it official.

decisions.choice: she wrote: Esther as the main writer
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine and singular, with Esther named first and Mordecai added after. The queen now writes with her own authority, as Mordecai had done before (9:20). She is named with her father, Abihail (2:15), as at her first appearance before the king.

decisions.choice: this second letter of Purim
alternatives: to confirm (a second time) the letter of Purim
decisions.reason: This most likely means a second letter, after Mordecai's (9:20), written to confirm the feast. It can also be read as confirming the earlier letter a second time.

decisions.choice: all authority: full power
decisions.reason: The word means power or strength; it is used of the king's might in 10:2.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סְפָרִ֜ים אֶל־כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֗ים אֶל־שֶׁ֨בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּמֵאָה֙ מְדִינָ֔ה מַלְכ֖וּת אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ דִּבְרֵ֥י שָׁל֖וֹם וֶאֱמֶֽת׃
records.gloss: And he sent letters to all the Jews, to [the] seven and twenty and hundred province[s], [the] kingdom of Ahasuerus, words of peace and truth,
pieces: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth,

L.30: And he sent letters to all the Jews, to the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, words of peace and truth,

R.30: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus. They were words of peace and truth,

decisions.choice: he sent: most likely Mordecai
decisions.reason: The verb is masculine singular. It most likely means Mordecai, named in verse 29; it may also be impersonal, "letters were sent".

decisions.choice: words of peace and truth: words of goodwill and assurance
decisions.reason: Peace is well-being and good relations; truth is faithfulness, words that can be relied on. The pair also appears in Zechariah 8:19, where fasts are to become feasts of joy, and in 2 Kings 20:19.

decisions.choice: 127 provinces
decisions.reason: The extent of Ahasuerus's empire, from India to Cush, as in 1:1 and 8:9.

decisions.choice: Mordecai
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the sender, following m1.

records.source: לְקַיֵּ֡ם אֵת־יְמֵי֩ הַפֻּרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה בִּזְמַנֵּיהֶ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ קִיַּ֨ם עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם מָרְדֳּכַ֤י הַיְּהוּדִי֙ וְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה וְכַאֲשֶׁ֛ר קִיְּמ֥וּ עַל־נַפְשָׁ֖ם וְעַל־זַרְעָ֑ם דִּבְרֵ֥י הַצֹּמ֖וֹת וְזַעֲקָתָֽם׃
records.gloss: to confirm [the] days of the Purim the these in their appointed times, as had established on them Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen, and as they had established on themselves and on their offspring, [the] matters of the fasts and their cry.
pieces: to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had ordered them, and as they had taken on themselves and their descendants the keeping of fasts and lamenting.

L.31: to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had established for themselves and for their descendants the matters of the fasts and their crying out.

R.31: to make the days of Purim official, to be kept at the right times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had commanded. The Jews had already agreed to this for themselves and their descendants, just as they had agreed to keep times of fasting and mourning.

decisions.choice: as they had established ... the matters of the fasts: the feast compared with fasts already kept
alternatives: the letter also fixed the fasts and laments that go with Purim
decisions.reason: The last words are hard to fit into the sentence. Most likely they mean that the Jews took on the feast of Purim just as they had already taken on days of fasting and mourning; it may instead mean that the letter also set rules for fasting along with the feast.

decisions.choice: the fasts and their cry
decisions.reason: The book has told of fasting and loud crying when Haman's decree went out (4:1-3) and of Esther's three-day fast (4:16). Jewish practice later kept a fast on the thirteenth of Adar, the day before Purim.

decisions.choice: fasting and mourning
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the matters of the fasts and their cry", a cry of distress as in 4:1-3. Readable folds this into "fasting and mourning" and, like the book itself, does not name God.

records.source: וּמַאֲמַ֣ר אֶסְתֵּ֔ר קִיַּ֕ם דִּבְרֵ֥י הַפֻּרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְנִכְתָּ֖ב בַּסֵּֽפֶר׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] command of Esther confirmed [the] matters of the Purim the these, and it was written in the book.
pieces: Esther's command confirmed these rules for Purim, and it was written down in the book.

L.32: And the command of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written in the book.

R.32: Esther's command made these rules for Purim official, and it was written down in a book.

decisions.choice: the matters of Purim: the rules for keeping Purim
decisions.reason: The word means words or matters; here, what Esther's letter laid down.

decisions.choice: written in the book: in a written record
decisions.reason: The text does not say which book. It may be a book of records, like the royal chronicles of 2:23, 6:1 and 10:2, or a scroll containing these rules.
